title: Create local voice clones for game characters
author: formicidfighter
selftext:
Hey everyone, we’re building a product at [aviad.ai](http://aviad.ai) that helps game devs create small, local voice clones that they can download and use for game characters.

You can use our tool to go from a few reference audio clips to high quality training data and a fully trained voice model quickly. We’re starting with finetunes that come out to around 800 MB. But are working on getting this much smaller in the coming weeks. You can listen to some examples on our website to get a sense for quality. We also have an update to our Unity package coming soon to easily integrate these models into the engine.

Our goal is to help game devs create fully voiced, dynamic characters that are very small and run on-device. We’re excited to see new types of game get made with characters like these.

If you want early access (will start onboarding folks to the product in the coming week), [join our Discord](https://discord.gg/Jk4jUYghnA)!

replies.author: PDeperson
replies.body: That's what I thought, haha. Looks like nowadays, using terms like "open source" and "local" gets companies more attention, and in reality, they are free but limited. 😂

replies.author: formicidfighter
replies.body: It's not gated by an API! You can download the models and use them however you like. 800 MB for now, but will get them smaller soon

replies.author: Termin8or9000
replies.body: Thank you for the explanation. Sorry, it wasn't that obvious from the thread.

comments.author: DigitalDokkaebi
comments.body: Is this 800 MB for a model that can do a suite of voices, or 800 MB for a single voice?

replies.author: formicidfighter
replies.body: For a single voice right now. We're working on Kokoro finetunes which will get the size much smaller
